tools.name: domain_report
tools.description: DNS, DNSSEC, email security, blocklists, certificates, HTTPS and registration in one report with a security grade (A+ to F) and what to fix first.

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Every record for a name from its authoritative nameservers or a public resolver, or one record compared across 13 resolvers worldwide.

tools.name: dnssec
tools.description: Is the zone signed, does the chain of trust validate, and are the algorithms current?

tools.name: nameserver_check
tools.description: Tests every nameserver of a domain directly: lame or unreachable servers, NS and glue mismatches, SOA serials, open recursion, TCP and EDNS.

tools.name: email_auth
tools.description: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT and BIMI graded, with the exact records to fix what is missing.

tools.name: email_headers
tools.description: Paste a message's headers to see its route and delays, SPF, DKIM and DMARC results with alignment, and why it may have gone to spam.

tools.name: email_record_builder
tools.description: Build an SPF record from the services that send your mail, or a DMARC record from a policy, and compare it with the one you publish now.

tools.name: blacklist
tools.description: Is an IP, a domain or its mail servers on the spam blocklists receivers use – and how to get delisted.

tools.name: ssl_check
tools.description: Certificate, chain, expiry, hostname match, key strength and the TLS version a server negotiates.

tools.name: http_headers
tools.description: Redirect chain, response headers and a graded check of HSTS, CSP and the other security headers.

tools.name: ct_search
tools.description: Every publicly logged certificate for a domain and its subdomains – find forgotten hosts and unexpected issuers.

tools.name: network_report
tools.description: Who holds an IP address, prefix or AS number, how it is routed (origin AS, RPKI, IRR), its reverse DNS, blocklist listings and PeeringDB record, with what to fix first.

tools.name: whois
tools.description: Who holds a domain, IP address or AS number – from the registry, via RDAP.

tools.name: bgp
tools.description: Origin AS, visibility, RPKI validity, upstreams and announced prefixes from the global routing table.

tools.name: rpki
tools.description: Whether a route is RPKI valid, invalid or not found, with the ROAs covering the prefix, max-length mistakes and how to fix them.

tools.name: peeringdb
tools.description: A network’s peering policy, internet exchange ports, facilities and NOC contacts from PeeringDB.

tools.name: reverse_dns
tools.description: The PTR name of an IP address, whether it resolves back to the same IP (FCrDNS), and whether it looks generic.

tools.name: port_check
tools.description: Whether a TCP port is open, closed or filtered from the internet, from one timed connection from our server.

tools.name: subnet_calculator
tools.description: Subnet ranges, masks and splits for IPv4 and IPv6, IPv6 and EUI-64 address details, and merging lists into the fewest CIDRs.

tools.name: mcp_server_test
tools.description: Connect to a remote MCP server like an AI assistant would: handshake, tools, resources, prompts, OAuth discovery and context cost, checked against the spec.

tools.name: jwt_decoder
tools.description: Decode a JSON Web Token's header and claims, check alg, exp, nbf and iat, and verify its signature if you give a key; the token is never stored.

tools.name: mac_lookup
tools.description: Who made a network card, from the IEEE registry – and whether the address is randomised.

tools.name: dn42_registry
tools.description: Look up any DN42 object – AS, IP, prefix, maintainer, person or .dn42 domain – with everything linked to it.

tools.name: dn42_free
tools.description: Unregistered AS numbers, free IPv4 blocks and a random unused IPv6 /48 – checked against the live registry.

tools.name: dn42_peering_config
tools.description: WireGuard, BIRD 2 and RouterOS 7 configs for a DN42 peering, following the wiki conventions.

tools.name: create_webhook_url
tools.description: Creates a public URL that records every request sent to it (webhooks, callbacks) for 7 days, and returns its bin id and key for the other webhook tools.

tools.name: list_webhook_requests
tools.description: Requests a webhook URL received, oldest first: pass after_id for only newer ones, and wait_seconds to wait briefly for the next.

tools.name: get_webhook_request
tools.description: One request received by a webhook URL in full (every header, the body, base64 if binary) with a curl command that sends it again.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_webhook_requests, get_webhook_request · Private data: dns_lookup, email_auth, email_record_builder, network_report, peeringdb, jwt_decoder, create_webhook_url · Public sink: domain_report, email_auth, email_headers, email_record_builder, create_webhook_url, list_webhook_requests, get_webhook_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_webhook_requests, get_webhook_request · Private data: dns_lookup, email_auth, email_record_builder, network_report, peeringdb, jwt_decoder, create_webhook_url · Public sink: domain_report, email_auth, email_headers, email_record_builder, create_webhook_url, list_webhook_requests, get_webhook_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
